concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 2 – Extended Feature Construction / Phase 3 – Feature Selection & Scaling / Phase 9 – Mann‑Whitney U & FDR
concerns.text: The plan selects the top‑500 features using a chi‑square filter (Phase 3) – a supervised, label‑dependent step – and then performs Mann‑Whitney U tests on those same features (Phase 9) to assess statistical significance. Because the same dataset and phenotype labels are used for both selection and testing, the significance assessment is not independent of the selection process, creating a circular ‘double‑dipping’ validation that can inflate false‑positive rates. A sound methodology would separate feature selection from significance testing, e.g., by using nested cross‑validation or a held‑out validation set for the Mann‑Whitney tests.
